approachQuestion.prompt:
A redundant physical loop. An undirected simple graph represents cables between devices. Return true if it contains a cycle: a closed route using at least three distinct vertices before returning to its start. A disconnected region can contain the only cycle.

Input: read-only adjacency lists for IDs 0..V-1; 1 <= V <= 200000 and 0 <= E <= 400000. Each cable appears at both endpoints, with no self-loops or parallel edges. Output one boolean.

Example 1: lists=[[1],[0],[]], output=false: the two entries describe one cable, not a cycle.
Example 2: lists=[[],[2,3],[1,3],[1,2]], output=true.

options.text: Traverse every unvisited component with an explicit stack, marking vertices when pushed and recording a parent. On an edge to an already visited vertex other than the current vertex’s parent, report a cycle.
options.feedback: The reverse entry of a tree edge is expected and must be ignored. Any other edge between discovered vertices closes a cycle in an undirected simple graph; the forest covers disconnected components.

options.text: Use a BFS forest with one visited array and parent per vertex. Reject the reverse edge to the parent; report a cycle on any other edge to a visited vertex.
options.feedback: The same tree-edge distinction works with queue order. Every component is examined and the resource bounds match the stack implementation.

options.text: Report a cycle whenever a traversal sees an edge whose other endpoint is already visited, including the parent.
options.feedback: For lists=[[1],[0]], exploration from 0 reaches 1, then sees the reverse entry 1->0 and falsely reports a cycle. It is just one undirected cable.

options.text: Use a correct parent-aware cycle traversal, but start only at vertex 0 and return false if that component has no cycle.
options.feedback: Example 2 has an isolated vertex 0 and a cycle among 1,2,3. Testing one component misses a legal cycle elsewhere.

feedback.reason: For an undirected graph, the parent edge is not evidence of a cycle. This differs from testing active-route back edges in a directed graph.
details: Initialize visited and parent arrays and scan all roots. For each unvisited root, assign a sentinel parent, mark and push it. Pop u and inspect its neighbors. Mark and push an unseen v with parent[v]=u. If v is already visited and v is not parent[u], return true. Return false after every component has been exhausted.
The edge back to a DFS parent is the same undirected connection, not evidence of a cycle. Any other already visited neighbor closes a loop under the simple-graph contract. Search every component.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze parent-aware-forest. V counts vertices and E simple undirected edges stored twice. Preallocate V-entry visited and parent arrays and a V-slot stack; initialize arrays and scan all roots. Indexing and push/pop take constant time. No hashing, recursion, shifting, amortized growth, or copying is used. Exclude input and scalar output; include working arrays and stack. Use worst case without an early cycle.
constraints: Choose the tightest standard worst-case bound for the specified implementation.

options.text: O(V + E) time, O(V) auxiliary space
O(V + E) time, O(1) auxiliary space
O(V(V + E)) time, O(V) auxiliary space
O(V + E) time, O(V + E) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Each vertex is scheduled once and both stored directions of each cable are inspected.
details: The option “O(V + E) time, O(V) auxiliary space” is tight: each vertex is pushed once, each of 2E adjacency entries is checked once, and arrays/root scans cost V. Parents, marks and stack use O(V). The option “O(V + E) time, O(1) auxiliary space” omits them. C unnecessarily repeats traversal from every vertex instead of retaining marks. The option “O(V + E) time, O(V + E) auxiliary space” counts edge copies although the supplied lists are directly inspected.
